clips.title: What is OTel? | OTel for Beginners - The JavaScript Journey
clips.why: The OpenTelemetry project's own short answer to what OTel is, aimed at JavaScript developers.
look: OTel is a standard and a set of tools, not a database or a dashboard.
The same signals, metrics, logs and traces, from any language, in one format.
Data goes to a backend of your choice, which for us is VictoriaMetrics and VictoriaLogs.
clips.after: Claude Code already produces OTel signals; our job is only to receive them safely.

clips.title: OpenTelemetry Collector: EVERYTHING you need to know [to get started]
clips.why: A clear walk through the collector's parts: receivers, processors, exporters, and the pipelines that wire them.
look: Receivers take data in, processors change it, exporters send it on.
Processors run in the order the pipeline lists them, which is why the scrub comes before any export.
A component only does something when a pipeline uses it.
clips.after: Our scrub is one processor in exactly this picture, and the lab's fix is what happens when the pipeline forgets to list it.

practice.q: Which signal fits "show every Bash command that failed in the build step of RH-1234, with its tool name"?

options.why: A metric could count the failures, but it has no room for the details of each one.
Each failure is one record with attributes such as tool_name, success and step. That is an event.
A trace follows one request across services. These are separate moments inside one session.

practice.q: Finish the pipeline so the scrub really runs on events.
practice.hint: The full name of the processor, type and name joined with a slash.
practice.why: A processor runs only when the pipeline lists it. Defined but unlisted, it does nothing, without any warning.

practice.q: Put the journey of one Claude Code event in order.
items: Claude Code sends the event over OTLP to the collector's address
The OTLP receiver accepts it on port 4318
The scrub processor deletes the prompt, the command and the email, and adds a hash
The exporter writes the scrubbed event to VictoriaLogs
Grafana shows it in a panel grouped by team and step
practice.why: Content is deleted in the middle step, before anything is written, so no store ever holds it.

practice.q: Why does the scrub add user.hash before it deletes user.email?

options.text: Because the hash is computed from the email, so the email must still be there
options.why: Statements run in order. Delete first and the hash statement finds nothing to hash.

options.text: Because OTLP requires a user attribute on every event
options.why: OTLP requires no user attribute. The hash is there so we can count users without names.

options.text: Because deleting is slow and must come last
options.why: Speed is not the reason. Order is about data: the hash needs the email as its input.

practice.q: Someone wants user.email as a label on the cost metric "to see who spends most". What is the problem?

options.why: They can. The problem is what the label means and how many values it has.

options.text: It is personal data in a store everyone can query, and one new series per person
options.why: We show numbers per team at most. A personal label is both a privacy problem and many more series to store.

options.text: The collector would drop the whole metric
options.why: Without our scrub it would pass. With it, the email is replaced by a hash before export.
